# editxr

> A WYSIWYG Markdown editor for the terminal. AI-assisted, 100% Swift, zero dependencies. macOS, Linux and Windows. Open source (MIT).

editxr renders Markdown live as you type — headings, lists, tables, and code are
styled in place in the terminal buffer, not in a split preview. The line under the
cursor stays raw, editable text. You can hand a whole section to an LLM and review
the change as an inline diff before it lands.

## What it does
- Live Markdown rendering in the terminal (WYSIWYG): headings, emphasis, lists, task lists, tables, blockquotes, code blocks, and YAML frontmatter.
- AI section editing: select a section, describe a change, and accept or reject it as a red/green inline diff. No chat thread; nothing is applied without approval.
- Obsidian-style linking: `[[wikilinks]]` and `[](file.md)` links render collapsed and open in a tab (Ctrl+]), with fuzzy file search (Ctrl+O) and back-navigation (Ctrl+[).
- Docked sidebars: a live outline of the document's headings, or a file explorer for the folder you opened.
- Bring your own model: LM Studio (local), OpenAI, OpenRouter, or an offline mock that needs no backend.
- 12 themes, light or dark, chosen from a command palette.
- Incremental find, HTML export, syntax highlighting, word wrap, and per-file cursor memory.
- Tables that stay aligned: glyph widths are measured from the live terminal, so emoji and ambiguous-width symbols don't break the columns.
- Native Swift binary with no runtime dependencies. Runs on macOS 12+, Linux, and Windows 10+.

## Install
- One line (downloads the prebuilt binary for your platform, falls back to source): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pixdeo/editxr/main/install.sh | bash`
- Homebrew: `brew install pixdeo/tap/editxr`
- Prebuilt packages on each release (https://github.com/pixdeo/editxr/releases):
  - macOS universal (signed & notarised): editxr-<version>-macos-universal.zip
  - Linux x86_64 (static musl, no dependencies): editxr-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
  - Linux aarch64 (static musl, no dependencies): editxr-<version>-linux-aarch64.tar.gz
  - Windows x64 (self-contained zip, also runs on Windows-on-ARM): editxr-<version>-windows-x64.zip
